title: Customer Onboarding: SLO–Contract Mapping and QBR Calibration
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable process for translating enterprise contract commitments (SLA / SLO clauses) into operational SLOs, telemetry contracts, alert thresholds, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) calibration agenda. It is intended for Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and EngOps stakeholders responsible for onboarding enterprise customers with Dedicated or Private deployments.

Goals:
- Ensure every contractual SLA/SLO has an unambiguous operational mapping to metrics and alerts.
- Produce a calibrated QBR agenda that highlights contractual compliance, trends, and actionable remediation steps.
- Reduce post-go-live churn caused by misaligned expectations between contract language and telemetry.

Scope and Audience:
- Scope: Redwood-hosted Dedicated and Private deployments; multi-tenant customers with contractual SLOs; QBRs for customers > $100k ARR.
- Audience: CSMs, SEs, EngOps, SRE liaison, customer technical leads.

Prerequisites (Before using this playbook):
1) Signed Service Agreement with SLO/SLA clauses and penalties.
2) Customer onboarded to telemetry forwarding (metrics + traces + logs) or Redwood-managed telemetry ingestion setup.
3) Assigned Redwood owners: CSM, SE, EngOps engineer, and Onsite/Customer success contact.

Definitions (short):
- SLA: Legal commitment in contract (uptime, response time guarantees).
- SLO: Operational objective measured by telemetry (e.g., p99 inference latency <= X ms).
- Error budget: Allowable window for SLO misses over evaluation period.
- Telemetry contract: The list of metrics, tags/labels, traces, and logs the customer and Redwood agree to exchange and retain.

1) One-page mapping template (mandatory)
Populate the following table and attach to the customer onboarding packet. Use concrete metric names and queries.

| Contract clause (verbatim) | Operational SLO (human) | Metric name | Aggregation/window | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| "API availability 99.95% monthly" | API availability >= 99.95% per calendar month | system.uptime.redwood-api | availability/month | < 99.95% -> P2 oncall + notify CSM | EngOps (api-team) |
| "Median latency under 120ms" | request.latency.p50 <= 120ms (rolling 7d) | request.latency.p50.redwood-api | p50/7d rolling | > 120ms for 30m -> P2 | Runtime Observability |
| "99th percentile inference latency < 2s" | inference.p99 < 2000ms (1h) | model.inference.latency.p99 | p99/1h | > 2000ms for 15m -> P1 | Serving Runtime |

Notes on the template: enter exact MQL/PromQL/SQL snippets in the Metric name field if available and store them in the customer telemetry folder.

2) Telemetry contract checklist (must be executed during provisioning)
- Metrics: availability, request.latencies (p50/p90/p95/p99), error rates, kvcache.hit_ratio, batch.size distribution, concurrency per tenant, token_count_per_request.
- Traces: end-to-end request traces spanning API gateway -> routing -> model runtime, with a correlation id (trace.customer_request_id).
- Logs: structured error logs with error.code, error.stage. Include sampling policy for debug-level logs for high-volume customers.
- Retention: default 90 days for metrics, 365 days for aggregations (QBR-ready), 30 days for full raw traces. Any deviation must be explicitly approved and added to the contract appendix.

3) QBR calibration agenda (recommended 60–75 minutes)
1. Executive summary (5m): usage, ARR impact, top 3 wins/risks.
2. SLO compliance snapshot (10m): last 90 days, error budget burn, recent misses. Attach the one-page SLO mapping.
3. Inference economics (10m): tokens/day, avg cost per 1k tokens, trends vs previous QBR, recommendation for batching/quantization if cost drift > 12%.
4. Reliability and incidents (10m): top incidents, actions completed, remaining mitigations.
5. Capacity and scaling plan (10m): autoscale behavior, reserved capacity headroom, burst strategy.
6. Roadmap alignment (10m): product features that affect customer (e.g., new caching, kernel upgrades), expected impact and rollback plan.
7. Action items and owner sign-off (10m): explicit owners and due dates.

Deliverables for the QBR: updated SLO table (signed off by customer and EngOps), runbook excerpts for any outstanding mitigations, and a 3-point action plan with owners and ETA.

4) Alert and incident escalation mapping (short matrix)
Use this matrix to set alert severity and who is paged. Insert these rows into the customer-specific alerting policy in PagerDuty/Opsgenie.

| Symptom | Metric/Query example | Severity | Page | Escalation path | Customer notification tier |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| High 99th inference latency | model.inference.latency.p99 > 2000ms (15m) | P1 | Serving-runtime oncall | 15m -> SRE lead -> Eng RTE | Notify CSM (1h) if sustained 30m |
| API availability drop | availability < 99.95% (1h) | P2 | EngOps oncall | 30m -> infra lead | Notify CSM (1h) and AE |
| Elevated error rate | request.errors.rate > 0.5% (rolling 10m) | P2 | Runtime Observability | 30m -> SE triage | Initial email to customer technical contact |

5) Example telemetry queries and alert rules (copy-paste)
- PromQL: 
  - request.latency.p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, job))
  - availability: 100 * sum(up{service=\"redwood-api\"}) / count(up{service=\"redwood-api\"})
- Example alert (pseudo-YAML):
  - alert: HighInferenceP99
    expr: model_inference_latency_p99{tenant_id=\"{{tenant}}\"} > 2.0
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: P1
    annotations:
      summary: \"{{tenant}}: inference p99 > 2s\"

6) Contractual reporting appendix (what to include in monthly/quarterly compliance reports)
- Monthly uptime statement (ISO-8601 month window) with calculation method.
- SLO evaluation windows and raw data snapshots (CSV of time buckets for the quarter).
- Incident summaries mapped to SLO impacts (time lost, segments affected).
- Any compensations/credits calculation with detailed math and applied time windows.

7) Calibration and dispute process (step-by-step)
1. Detection: Customer or Redwood flags an SLO miss in QBR or via support channel.
2. Evidence collection (3 business days): EngOps exports raw telemetry, traces, and logs for the evaluation window. Owner: EngOps.
3. Analysis (5 business days): Runtime and SE analyze root cause and propose whether the miss is operational (Redwood responsibility) or customer-caused (network, tenant misuse).
4. Reconciliation (2 business days): Finance and Legal calculate credits if applicable.
5. Remediation and closure (ongoing): Implement runbook fixes, monitoring changes, and calendar follow-up in next QBR.

8) Runbook excerpts (examples to add to customer runbook)
- Safe degrade: automatically route to lower-capacity model variant when p99 > 2s for 10m (fallback policy ID: fallback-model-2025).
- Emergency quiesce: reduce non-essential batch jobs and dev-tier traffic during major capacity incidents.
- KV cache warmup: after model rollout, run cache-warmup script for top N prefixes (script path: /opt/ops/cache-warmup.sh).

9) Ownership and sign-off checklist (onboarding gate)
- CSM: Confirm SLO mapping table reviewed with customer.
- SE: Validate telemetry queries and access.
- EngOps: Configure alerts and retention settings.
- SRE liaison: Approve escalation matrix and on-call routing.
- Customer: Sign-off on one-page SLO mapping and QBR cadence.

10) Templates and attachments (references)
- One-page SLO mapping template (CSV).
- QBR slide template (PPTX).
- Example PromQL/SQL snippets (TEXT).
- Sample incident-to-SLO impact worksheet (XLSX).
